nodes.name: Caucasian rhododendron
nodes.desc: A low evergreen shrub of the high Caucasus, known as the Georgian snow rose. Its alpine scrub is the open-slope habitat the Caucasian grouse favours.

nodes.name: Alpine meadow grasses
nodes.desc: Highland grasses and herbs that cover the meadows above the tree line in summer and feed grazers such as chamois.

nodes.name: Alpine wildflowers
nodes.desc: Gentians and other flowering herbs, among the best-recorded plants near the park, that colour the summer meadows.

nodes.name: Oriental spruce
nodes.desc: A conifer of the Caucasus forests. Winter-feeding chamois use conifer needles and bark, and squirrels take conifer seed.

nodes.name: Oriental beech
nodes.desc: A broadleaf forest tree of the Black Sea slopes whose nuts are food for dormice, squirrels and wild boar.

nodes.name: Chamois
nodes.desc: Eats highland grasses and herbs in summer and conifer needles and bark in winter. The Anatolian subspecies lives in Turkey.

nodes.name: European roe deer
nodes.desc: A small forest deer and prey for the region's lynx, wolves and bears.

nodes.name: Feral goat
nodes.desc: Goats graze the mountain slopes and are reported living wild in the range. Large carnivores take them.

nodes.name: Caucasian grouse
nodes.desc: A sedentary Near Threatened bird of open slopes with low rhododendron scrub beside broadleaf forest in the Pontic Mountains.

nodes.name: Caucasian squirrel
nodes.desc: A tree squirrel of the northeastern forests that feeds on seeds and nuts.

nodes.name: Edible dormouse
nodes.desc: A nocturnal tree-climbing rodent that eats nuts, seeds and fruit, and is hunted by foxes and lynx.

nodes.name: Wild boar
nodes.desc: An omnivore of the forests, rooting for nuts, roots and small animals, and listed among the range's large mammals.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: A generalist hunter of small mammals and birds that also takes carrion.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: A scavenger that feeds on carcasses of mountain ungulates, often alongside larger carnivores.

nodes.name: Bearded vulture
nodes.desc: A mountain vulture recorded near the park that feeds mainly on the bones and remains of dead animals.

nodes.name: Brown bear
nodes.desc: An omnivore taking most of its energy from plants but also hunting and scavenging; the Eastern Black Sea region holds Turkey's bears.

nodes.name: Gray wolf
nodes.desc: Pack hunter listed among the range's large mammals and a historic predator of chamois.

nodes.name: Eurasian lynx
nodes.desc: A solitary cat that preys on chamois, roe deer and smaller animals in forest and rocky terrain.

nodes.name: Summer sun
nodes.desc: Short alpine summers drive the growth of meadows and scrub above the tree line.

nodes.name: Snowpack & glaciers
nodes.desc: The range is heavily glaciated; winter snow and meltwater feed the meadows and mountain lakes.

nodes.name: Black Sea rain
nodes.desc: Moist air from the Black Sea coast waters the northern slopes and supports their forests.

nodes.name: Mountain soil
nodes.desc: Thin mountain soils hold nutrients returned by dead plants and animals.

nodes.name: Fungi & soil microbes
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants, dung and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.
